parameters.name: phi_per_OD
parameters.note: Total E. coli volume per unit OD600.
parameters.source_note: Measured directly across 22 growth conditions: 1 mL at OD600 = 1 holds about 3.6 uL of cells, with 2.4 to 4.5 uL across individual conditions. This project previously carried 8e-4, a textbook estimate of 8e8 cells per mL at 1 um3 each, which is 4.5x low because growing cells are larger than that. The model treats the whole cell volume as the cytoplasmic compartment, so it overstates the cytoplasm by the periplasmic fraction.

parameters.name: peri_frac
parameters.note: Periplasm as a fraction of cell volume.
parameters.source_note: No source is recorded for it in this project; it is the standard fraction.

parameters.name: k_mem
parameters.note: Cytoplasm-medium H2O2 exchange, P*(S/V).
parameters.source_note: The membrane permeability coefficient of 1.6e-3 cm/s reported in this work, times a surface-to-volume ratio of about 6 per um for an E. coli cell.

parameters.name: k_scav
parameters.note: Intracellular H2O2 scavenging by KatG/KatE/AhpCF in the wild type.
parameters.source_note: Not measured directly. Forced by two measurements in this work: a production rate of 14 uM/s against a resting cytoplasmic level of about 0.02 uM gives 700 /s.

parameters.name: k_scav_knockout
parameters.note: Residual scavenging in a catalase/peroxidase triple knockout (Hpx-). Used only to test whether a type-A candidate needs the knockout to pass.
parameters.source_note: Chosen so a catalase/peroxidase triple knockout rests near 2.8 uM. Used only to test whether a candidate would need the knockout, never as a measurement.

parameters.name: P_endo
parameters.note: Endogenous cytoplasmic H2O2 production in a growing culture.
parameters.source_note: Measured directly in aerobically growing cells.

parameters.name: k_chem
parameters.note: Chemical H2O2 loss in the medium. Zero unless the sample matrix contributes.
parameters.source_note: Set to zero. A sample matrix that destroys peroxide would make this positive, and none of the studies reports it.

parameters.name: K_oxyr
parameters.note: Cytoplasmic H2O2 at half OxyR activation.
parameters.source_note: In vitro titration: 0.1 uM oxidised half the purified protein within 30 s, and 0.05 to 0.2 uM did so across conditions. The same work needed 5 uM outside the cell for the same effect in vivo, which this model carries separately as k_scav rather than folding it into K.

parameters.name: n_hill
parameters.note: Hill coefficient of OxyR activation.
parameters.source_note: Non-cooperative. OxyR is a dimer of dimers and could be cooperative; no source in this project measures it.

parameters.name: beta
parameters.note: Promoter output at full OxyR activation.
parameters.source_note: Sets the signal scale, not the fold between two samples, which is what every verdict uses.

parameters.name: leak
parameters.note: Basal promoter output.
parameters.source_note: Sets the blank, not the fold between two samples.

parameters.name: gfp_maturation_halflife_s
parameters.note: sfGFP maturation half-life. k_mat = ln2 / this.
parameters.source_note: Measured in living E. coli by time-lapse: sfGFP reaches half maturation in 13.6 +/- 0.9 min at 37 C, and 19.4 min at 32 C. This project previously carried 360 s, which is 2.3x fast. The assay temperature is not fixed by the scenario, so the 37 C value is used and the 32 C one is the obvious sensitivity.

parameters.name: growth_doubling_pre_s
parameters.note: Doubling time before the assay. mu_pre = ln2 / this.
parameters.source_note: An operating condition of the assay, not a property of anything.

parameters.name: growth_doubling_s
parameters.note: Doubling time during the assay. mu = ln2 / this.
parameters.source_note: An operating condition of the assay, not a property of anything.

parameters.name: cv_reader
parameters.note: Relative SD of a single fluorescence measurement.
parameters.source_note: The reader this screen assumes. It sets the limit of detection, so the sensitivity analysis varies it.

parameters.name: n_rep
parameters.note: Technical replicates.

parameters.name: creatinine_MW_g_per_mol
parameters.note: Molar mass of creatinine. Converts creatinine g/L to mol/L for the per-mol-creatinine units.

parameters.name: hill_n_binding
parameters.note: Hill coefficient assumed for module types B and C. Modelling assumption, not a measured constant: 1.0 means non-cooperative single-site binding. No source reports a Hill coefficient for any sensor in sensors.csv.
parameters.source_note: No source reports a Hill coefficient for any sensor in sensors.csv.

parameters.name: z_required
parameters.note: Z needed to call two fluorescence readings separable at the reader.

parameters.name: auc_pass_min
parameters.note: Reported AUC at or above which stage 1 passes on the AUC route.

parameters.name: p_pass_max
parameters.note: Two-sided Welch p below which stage 1 can pass on the statistics route.

parameters.name: cohens_d_pass_min
parameters.note: Absolute Cohen's d required alongside the p-value. Both are needed, so a tiny effect at huge n does not pass.

parameters.name: sd_over_value_max
parameters.note: Applies only to an SD reconstructed from a range or an IQR. If that SD exceeds the central value by more than this, the strictly positive quantity cannot be anywhere near normal, the reconstruction is not trustworthy, and the row is called insufficient rather than failed. A spread the authors reported directly as an SD or SEM is never second-guessed this way.

parameters.name: conc_factor_max
parameters.note: Largest sample concentration factor considered achievable. Above this a candidate is red rather than yellow.

parameters.name: kd_ratio_lo
parameters.note: Analyte/Kd below this is called below-Kd: the sensor sits in its dead zone.

parameters.name: kd_ratio_hi
parameters.note: Analyte/Kd above this is called saturated.

parameters.name: conversion_target
parameters.note: Fraction of the analyte that must be turned over inside the read time. Sets the minimum enzyme loading reported by the enzyme comparison.

parameters.name: knockout_gain_min
parameters.note: Relative fold improvement a scavenger knockout must give before it is called helpful, rather than noise in the integration.

parameters.name: panel_rho_independent
parameters.note: Correlation assumed between markers from unrelated pathways. The optimistic bound on a panel: markers carry independent information.

parameters.name: panel_rho_correlated
parameters.note: Correlation assumed between markers of the same pathway, such as putrescine, spermidine and spermine, which share the polyamine biosynthetic route. The pessimistic bound. Neither value is measured: no source in clinical.csv reports a covariance between markers in the same patients, so panels are reported as a range between these two and never as a point estimate.

parameters.name: panel_max_size
parameters.note: Largest panel considered. Beyond this the combinatorics stop being informative given how few modules clear stage 2.

sensors.notes: Working value. Km given as 3.1e-4 M. The same paper also reports 83 uM in a different buffer, carried as a separate row. kcat/Km = 0.51 /uM/s.
Second published Km from the same paper (colorimetric assay buffer). Kept for the robustness sweep, not for the headline number. kcat/Km = 1.90 /uM/s.
Highest catalytic efficiency on DAS: kcat/Km = 72.2 /uM/s, 142x DhaPAO at Km 310.
kcat/Km = 1.63 /uM/s. Lower kcat and tighter Km than OpaPAO1.

No Km or kcat reported, so no calculation is possible from this row. Reported LOD 0.25 uM DAS, analytical range 0-10 and 0-1 uM, R2 0.94 and 0.91. UniProt not reported; the source sheet guessed A9E360 but the paper does not state it, so the field is empty.

EC 1.4.3.10. Soluble dimeric flavoprotein, 50 kDa subunits, non-covalent FAD. Putrescine is its best substrate of those tested. kcat/Km = 3.17 /uM/s, six times DhaPAO on DAS. Km 8.2 uM sits inside the urinary clinical range, which no other module here manages. Accepts longer polyamines, so spermidine and spermine are expected cross-reactants; short diamines and monoamines inhibit. t1/2 at 50 C is 2 h.

Monomeric sarcosine oxidase, Protein ID BAA03967, MW 43836 Da with FAD. Table 2 wild type: Km 17 +/- 2.6 mM, kcat 25 +/- 2.9 /s, specific activity 29 +/- 3.4 U/mg. kcat/Km = 0.0015 /uM/s, the weakest module in this table by three orders. Urinary sarcosine is micromolar, so the analyte sits about 1800x below Km: first order and far from saturation, but it needs correspondingly more enzyme. Assay by 4-aminoantipyrine/peroxidase at pH 8.0, 37 C.

EC 1.1.3.17. Table 1, fully oxidised FAD: kcat 61 +/- 6 /s, Ka 1.7 +/- 0.3 mM, kcat/Ka 36000 +/- 6400 /M/s. The paper reports Ka, the Michaelis constant for choline at saturating oxygen in a sequential mechanism, not a classical Km; below saturation the relevant quantity is kcat/Ka = 0.036 /uM/s, which is what this screen uses. KO2 703 +/- 102 uM. Measured at pH 7, 25 C.

EC 1.1.3.2, FMN-dependent. Wild type: kcat 88 +/- 2 /s, Km 0.50 +/- 0.10 mM, kcat/Km 176 +/- 31.2 /mM/s = 0.176 /uM/s. Measured air-saturated at [O2] 250 uM, pH 6.5, 20 C; Km for O2 about 51 uM, so oxygen was near-saturating. Tyr215 variants are published if a tighter Km is wanted: Y215F has Km 0.13 mM at kcat 22 /s.

No numerical Kd in this paper. Two web searches on 2026-10-06 found none elsewhere either, but that is a failed search rather than proof of absence. Gel-shift titration used 0, 10, 50 and 100 mM putrescine, roughly three orders of magnitude above urinary clinical levels. Spermidine had little or no effect, so selectivity over spermidine is plausible. The type A route to putrescine (PuORh) is quantified and this one is not.

AraC-family sarcosine-responsive activator of the sox operon. Confirmed sarcosine-responsive by beta-galactosidase reporter at 1 mM sarcosine and by EMSA, but no numerical ligand Kd is reported. Induction is specific: glycine betaine, dimethylglycine, glycine and pyruvate all fail to induce, so selectivity looks good but is unquantified. Activator, not a derepressed repressor.

Repressor; choline binding stimulates BetI-DNA complex formation. Reported Kd range 90-120 nM; the low end is entered and the range recorded here rather than averaged. Measured at pH 9.0 in 10 mM Tris-HCl with binding on ice, far from assay conditions, so the number should be treated as an order of magnitude. The only type B module in this table with any numerical constant.

Native lactate-responsive regulator. The cited paper characterises an engineered fluorescent sensor built on the LldR binding domain, not LldR acting as a transcription factor, so its Kd belongs to the fusion protein and is not entered here. No Kd for LldR as a repressor was found.
